paragraphs.text: Bruel et al. (2023) described the oral-facial-digital syndromes (OFDS) as a group of clinically and genetically heterogeneous disorders. They are characterized by defects in the development of the face and oral cavity, along with digit anomalies. They are ciliopathies: pathogenic variants in genes encoding ciliary proteins cause OFDS through deleterious structural or functional impacts on primary cilia (Bruel et al., 2023). Bruel et al. (2023) described a novel form of OFDS accompanied by cardiac, cerebral, skeletal, and anorectal defects.
